clis.advanced.asks.desc: What its screen shows when it asks you something: the agent waits for you, and nothing is typed into it meanwhile. Wrong, a question could be answered by what Combwork types.
clis.advanced.asks.title: Screen: asks you something
clis.advanced.osc7501.desc: The terminal sequence it writes its turn’s state in (OSC 7501), its first group the state (working, idle). Wrong, its status is read from its screen alone.
clis.advanced.osc7501.title: Terminal: its turn’s state
clis.advanced.ready.desc: What its screen shows when it is ready for a line: Combwork types the first prompt then, and shows it ready. Wrong, it shows as working and nothing is typed into it.
clis.advanced.ready.title: Screen: ready for a line
clis.advanced.titleAsks.desc: What its terminal title says when it asks you something. Wrong, the agent doesn’t show as waiting for you when it does.
clis.advanced.titleAsks.title: Title: asks you something
clis.advanced.version.desc: Where its version is in what its version command prints: the first group. Wrong, Provider Setup shows no version.
clis.advanced.version.title: Its version
clis.advanced.working.desc: What its screen shows while it works on a turn. Wrong, Combwork may show it idle while it works, or the other way round.
clis.advanced.working.title: Screen: working
clis.gaps.heading: {cli} runs from a description, so it has:
clis.note.install: It runs from a description in your Combwork folder (clis): install it yourself, then Reload in Settings → Providers → Your own CLIs.
clis.note.signIn: Sign it in as its own documentation says, in a terminal: Combwork runs no sign-in for it.
clis.problem.badEnv: “launch.env” can’t set {name}: {why, select, name {it isn’t a variable’s name} combwork {Combwork’s own variables (CW_…) are Combwork’s} other {}}.
clis.problem.badId: “id” must be lower case letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter (2 to 31 characters).
clis.problem.badMode: “launch.modes” has a mode {value} that isn’t a short lower-case name, or is given twice.
clis.problem.badSeconds: “{field}” must be a number of seconds from {min} to {max}.
clis.problem.badType: “{field}” must be {kind, select, text {text} list {a list of texts} object {an object} yesNo {true or false} other {{kind}}}.
clis.problem.duplicate: Its id {id} is also in {other}: neither is used.
clis.problem.fileTooBig: It is larger than {max, number} bytes.
clis.problem.keyInArgs: “server.args” can’t name '{key}': a key goes in a variable, never on a command line others can see.
clis.problem.noBaseUrl: “server” must name '{baseUrl}' in a variable or an argument.
clis.problem.noPrompt: “launch.prompt” must be 'typed', or an object whose 'arg' names '{prompt}'.
clis.problem.notObject: It isn’t a description: a JSON object is expected.
clis.problem.tooManyFiles: Only the first {max, number} descriptions are read: this one is left out.
clis.readiness.notFound: {provider} isn’t found: install it yourself (its description names where it is looked for), then choose Check again.
clis.settings.heading: Your own CLIs
clis.settings.lastGood: {file} has a problem; its last good version stays in use until it is fixed:
clis.settings.reloaded: {n, plural, =0 {No CLIs from descriptions} one {# CLI from a description} other {# CLIs from descriptions}}{problems, plural, =0 {} one {; # description not used} other {; # descriptions not used}}
clis.settings.what: A CLI with no provider of its own runs from a description: a JSON file in the clis folder of your Combwork profile. Combwork reads its status from its screen, and never changes its own config.
